features.title: Build the .deb, .rpm and Arch package with nfpm from one file list
features.description: `just package` builds the release binaries and then exactly one .deb, one .rpm and one .pkg.tar.zst (x86_64) into target/packages from a single nfpm configuration that lists every installed file once (source, destination, mode, owner): the service, the CLI, the PKCS#11 module, the systemd unit, the sysusers file, the D-Bus policy and activation files, the polkit action, the p11-kit module file and the journal catalog, all under /usr and nothing in /etc or /var. The service moves from /usr/libexec/custodiod to /usr/lib/custodio/custodiod in all three formats (open question 'Arch and /usr/libexec', option (a), which the person approving this list confirms), with the unit and the D-Bus activation file updated, so there is one unit and one activation file. Per-format overrides hold only metadata, dependency names (polkitd on the .deb, polkit on .rpm and Arch; systemd, the system bus, p11-kit and every shared library the binaries link, since nfpm does not compute them like cargo deb's $auto did) and, where the format can express it, polkit >= 124. Each format has its own lifecycle script files; until F43 and F44 they only do what the M1 postinst does. The recipe fails if any package is missing or if any file of the list is missing from a package. Versions: Debian revision, RPM release and Arch pkgrel are derived from the workspace version, and the recipe accepts a version override so a test can build an N+1 package from the same tree; recorded in docs/decisions.md. nfpm is pinned in mise.toml (with a checksum where mise supports one) and installed in harness/Containerfile; cargo-deb, the [package.metadata.deb] section, data/debian and every use of `cargo deb` leave the repository, mise.toml, the dev image and CI. The `shell_scripts` list that `just lint` passes to shellcheck covers the maintainer scripts whatever their file names.
features.verify: just check && just package && test $(ls target/packages/*.deb | wc -l) -eq 1 && test $(ls target/packages/*.rpm | wc -l) -eq 1 && test $(ls target/packages/*.pkg.tar.zst | wc -l) -eq 1 && ! grep -rqs 'package.metadata.deb' crates Cargo.toml && ! grep -rqsE 'cargo[- ]deb' justfile mise.toml harness/Containerfile .github && ! grep -rqs '/usr/libexec' data

features.title: Package parity and C library ceiling gates
features.description: Two new recipes, also run by `just package-gates` (which `check-slow` and CI include, each package gate as its own CI job or step): `just package-parity` lists the installed paths, modes and owners of the three packages in target/packages and fails if they differ, apart from the differences listed in a committed file in the repository where each entry has a reason (expected to be empty after F36). `just glibc-ceiling` reads every ELF file in every package and fails if any of them needs a glibc symbol version newer than the oldest glibc among the targets the packages install on, including Ubuntu 24.04 and Alma 10 (2.39 unless the builder finds otherwise; the ceiling and its source are recorded in the repository). How the build meets the ceiling is the builder's choice, and it must work in the dev container. Each gate has a self-test that a fabricated difference or a too-new symbol version makes it fail.
features.verify: just check && just package && just package-parity && just glibc-ceiling

features.title: Package linters with justified exception lists
features.description: `just package-lint` (part of `just package-gates`) runs lintian on the .deb, rpmlint on the .rpm and namcap on the .pkg.tar.zst. The three linters are installed in the dev image (harness/Containerfile), pinned where the source allows; on a host that lacks one, the recipe runs it in a container of the target distribution. Any finding fails the check unless it is in a committed exception list for that linter where each entry has a reason. The findings are fixed in the packaging where possible rather than listed; the path chosen in F36 is confirmed to be accepted by namcap and rpmlint, or the open question is reported in BLOCKED.md.
features.verify: just check && just package && just package-lint

features.title: custodiod refuses a Sign call whose bus credentials lack ProcessFD
features.description: When custodiod reads the caller's connection credentials for a Sign call it also asks for ProcessFD. If the bus does not return it, the signature is refused before polkit is asked, and the call leaves exactly one M1 journal entry with the 'authorization not possible' outcome. No D-Bus interface or audit field name changes; any added field follows the additive-change rule of docs/audit.md. Integration tests (in `just test-integration`) show that a Sign call whose credentials lack ProcessFD returns no signature, does not ask the fake polkit authority, and leaves exactly one journal entry with that outcome. The credential-reading code stays in the files `just mutants` covers, with no surviving mutant.
features.verify: just check && just test-integration && just mutants

features.title: Cross-check that the caller's pidfd and pid name the same process
features.description: Where it can be done without loosening custodio.service, custodiod checks that the pidfd from ProcessFD and the reported pid name the same process (docs/findings.md M1.2), and a mismatch is refused exactly like missing ProcessFD (no polkit query, one 'authorization not possible' entry), with tests. The exposure gate keeps its threshold. If the cross-check cannot be done within the current hardening, the presence check of F39 alone stays the requirement and the reason is recorded in docs/decisions.md, with a test or check that the unit was not loosened.
features.verify: just check && just test-integration && just mutants

features.title: Confirm whether polkit 124 reads ProcessFD from the bus
features.description: Before any Ubuntu 24.04 work, polkit 124's system-bus-name subject code is read (through a subagent) to establish whether it takes the pidfd from the bus's ProcessFD credential or falls back to the PID. The result, with the source files and versions read, goes in docs/findings.md under a section naming polkit 124 and ProcessFD. If 124 falls short, the minimum polkit declared by the packages is raised to the first release that does read it, Ubuntu 24.04 is dropped from the supported set in the docs and the e2e matrix, and BLOCKED.md asks the person approving the milestone to confirm.
features.verify: grep -qE '^#+ .*polkit 124' docs/findings.md && grep -q 'ProcessFD' docs/findings.md

features.title: Install-time check that the system bus provides ProcessFD
features.description: Before a package changes anything, its pre-install script (the same POSIX shell check shared by the three formats) asks the running system bus for its own connection credentials and fails the installation if ProcessFD is missing (on Arch, where pacman ignores a failing pre_install, the first installation only prints the message and a PreTransaction hook with AbortOnFail shipped in the package refuses every later upgrade and reinstall), with a message that names the missing ProcessFD support and points to the installation documentation (docs/install.md, written in F51; on Ubuntu 24.04: switch to dbus-broker and reboot). It tests the capability, never the daemon name or distribution. When no system bus is running (chroot, image build, rpm-ostree), it installs anyway and prints a notice that the service will refuse to sign until a bus with ProcessFD runs (open question 'Installing without a running bus', proposed answer). `just test-scripts` (new recipe, part of `just check`) tests the check against a private dbus-daemon of the dev container (which has ProcessFD, so it passes), against a bus or stub that omits ProcessFD (refused, non-zero exit, message), and with no bus (notice, success).
features.verify: just check && just package && just package-lint

features.title: Lifecycle scripts of the .deb: install, upgrade, remove, purge
features.description: The .deb's preinst, postinst, prerm and postrm implement SPEC design section 2 with Debian's conventions (behaviour of dh_installsystemd and dh_installsysusers, not their text): on install, create the custodio account from the sysusers file before the bus policy is loaded, daemon-reload, reload the bus, update the journal catalog, never enable or start the unit, never touch the state directory; on upgrade, keep the state directory and account and restart the service once the new files and bus policy are in place only if it was running; on remove and on purge, stop the service, keep the state directory and the account, and print where the keys are and that deleting them by hand destroys them for good. No script deletes, chowns, chmods, reads, copies or prints anything under the state directory, or widens the bus policy, polkit action or unit hardening. Upgrading from the last cargo-deb .deb (whose only script is the M1 postinst) is handled as a normal upgrade. `just test-scripts` runs each script with stubbed systemctl, systemd-sysusers, journalctl and bus tools on a temporary root, and asserts the calls made and that a populated state directory is byte-identical with the same owner and modes after upgrade, remove and purge.
features.verify: just check && just package && just package-lint

features.title: Lifecycle scripts of the .rpm
features.description: The .rpm scriptlets (behaviour of %systemd_post, %systemd_preun, %systemd_postun_with_restart and Fedora's sysusers handling) implement the same install, upgrade and removal decisions as F43: account before the bus policy, daemon-reload, bus reload, catalog update, no enable or start, restart on upgrade only if running, state directory and account kept on removal (including rpm-ostree uninstall) with the same notice, and no script touching the state directory or widening the policy, action or hardening. Scriptlets must tolerate running offline (rpm-ostree: no bus, read-only /var). `just test-scripts` covers them like the .deb scripts, including the RPM argument counts for install, upgrade and erase.
features.verify: just check && just package && just package-lint

features.title: Lifecycle scripts of the Arch package
features.description: The Arch install script (behaviour of systemd's pacman hooks, without duplicating what the hooks already do) implements the same install, upgrade and removal decisions as F43: account before the bus policy, daemon-reload, bus reload, catalog update, no enable or start, restart on upgrade only if running, state directory and account kept on removal with the same notice, and no script touching the state directory or widening the policy, action or hardening. It keeps F42's pre_install and pre_upgrade check and PreTransaction hook. `just test-scripts` covers post_install, post_upgrade, pre_remove and post_remove like the .deb scripts.
features.verify: just check && just package && just package-lint

features.title: End-to-end harness per target, with Debian 13
features.description: `just e2e <target>` (or `just e2e all`, the default) builds the packages, boots a privileged systemd container of the target from e2e/targets/<target>/Containerfile with the distribution's real polkit and its default system bus daemon, installs the package with the target's own tool (apt/dpkg here; never by copying files, and the image never contains the package) and runs the existing suite through one shared guest script. Each run prints and saves which bus daemon and polkit version it used. Target debian13 exists; adding a target is a new directory. Each target has a committed skip list (case and reason); the suite fails if any case is skipped that is not on that target's list, and `just test-scripts` tests that enforcement.
features.verify: just check && bash -n e2e/*.sh && test -f e2e/targets/debian13/Containerfile && test -f e2e/targets/debian13/skip.list && grep -rqi 'polkit' e2e/targets

features.title: Administrator documentation for installing and removing
features.description: docs/install.md explains: installing on Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04, Fedora 44, RHEL/Alma 10 and Arch with each system's tool, and on rpm-ostree systems by layering; why a bus without ProcessFD is refused; how to switch Ubuntu 24.04 to dbus-broker and reboot (unless F41 dropped Ubuntu 24.04); what removal and purge leave behind (state directory, keys, custodio account) and the manual command that destroys the keys deliberately, with the warning that deletion is not secure erasure; that a signature waiting for polkit during an upgrade fails closed; and how to check that journald storage is persistent and why it matters for the audit trail (the package does not change journald's configuration). features.title: The service binary where each distribution wants it
features.description: Each package installs the service where its distribution's guidelines put internal binaries: /usr/libexec/custodio/custodiod in the .deb and the .rpm, /usr/lib/custodio/custodiod in the Arch package, the difference listed in packaging/parity-exceptions.txt with its reason. The unit's ExecStart follows each path from one source file. Why, recorded in docs/decisions.md in place of the 2026-10-30 entry: on Fedora /usr/lib/custodio is labelled lib_t, so systemd leaves the service in init_t, systemd's own domain, and the key files it writes get init_var_lib_t (seen in F54 and F55); from /usr/libexec (bin_t) it runs in unconfined_service_t, as SPEC expects. Upgrading from a package with the old path keeps the keys and the service starts from the new path; on installations upgraded from it, key files written under init_t get their default label (var_lib_t) back, also when the .rpm is layered with rpm-ostree. The package gates and lintian, rpmlint and namcap accept the three packages.
features.verify: just check && just package-gates && bash -n e2e/*.sh && grep -q '/usr/libexec/custodio/custodiod' packaging/nfpm.yaml && grep -q '/usr/lib/custodio/custodiod' packaging/parity-exceptions.txt && grep -q 'unconfined_service_t' docs/decisions.md

features.title: SELinux domain by hand: fedora44 and bazzite after the move
features.description: After F61, on a host with a container engine `just e2e all` passes on every target. On fedora44 (dnf) and on bazzite (rpm-ostree, with a reboot), starting from the 0.1.0 package with the old path and keys imported under it, then upgrading to the new package: custodiod runs as unconfined_service_t (ps -eZ), the key files carry var_lib_t, the same keys sign with the polkit dialog without a new import and a cancel makes the signature fail, and no SELinux denial involves the service, polkit or the module. The run is recorded in docs/findings.md.
